comparisonBoundary: Final ContentProcessor.getContent result with includeTitle=false, including its paragraph shaping loop (ContentProcessor.kt:185-201); titles use BookChapter.getDisplayTitle. The frozen replacement insertion quotes the JavaScript result with Matcher.quoteReplacement (RegexExtensions.kt:38-40).
capabilityRows: A an enabled @js: replacement returned text, evaluated once per match (ContentProcessor.getContent -> CharSequence.replace, RegexExtensions.kt:23-64)
B the replacement bindings and the insertion semantics: the complete match is `result`, captures are derived by the script, and $1/${name}/\1 in the returned text are inserted literally
C a literal (non-@js:) replacement applied in the same rule set, in sortOrder, with the @js: ones, plus a literal rule whose replacement text starts with `@js:`
D a disabled @js: rule is not selected and not executed
E a script that throws keeps the content and is reported
F a script that exceeds its rule deadline disables the rule and follows the frozen timeout side effect
G the four @js: replacement rules of the operator 2026-09-17 backup, seeded exactly as the backup holds them

acceptedDivergences.summary: Timeout side effect: frozen injects the rule name plus the exception text into the content and schedules an application restart; the product disables the rule, reports it and preserves the original text.
acceptedDivergences.product: PASS-by-policy: report, disable, keep original text (ADR 0011).
acceptedDivergences.frozen: recorded verbatim in the golden content and in rulesDisabledByRun.

acceptedDivergences.summary: Binding breadth: frozen injects only the complete match as `result`; the product evaluates through the approved source script facade, whose documented globals are broader.
Error reporting channel, not content: frozen logs to AppLog and toasts; the product reports a notice. Content and rule state are equal.
acceptedDivergences.frozen: not observable from the harness; the content is the compared value.

coverageGaps: The four operator backup rules are disabled in the backup, so this corpus records `disabled; replacement not executed` for each. Their enabled execution stays unobserved; the corpus carries each rule verbatim so that a later ticket can seed them enabled.

The frozen timeout row is a single call: it observes the disabled rule and the injected content, but a completed instrumentation cannot demonstrate the 3 s application restart (RegexExtensions.kt:51-58). ADR 0011 sampled-deadline limits still apply to the product side.
The frozen restart and the frozen injected diagnostic text stay an accepted divergence; they are not normalized into a pass.
Cancel-during-replacement and the product reader cancellation path are covered by test/content_processing_test.dart, not by this device corpus.
The backup rules are title-scope (id 1) and content-scope (ids 2-4); no enabled title-scope backup script is executed here.

The row records both binding surfaces exactly; it is not normalized into a pass.

cases.policy: ADR 0011 / #17 policy row: the frozen reader disables the timed-out rule and replaces the content with the rule name plus the timeout exception text (ContentProcessor.kt:169-171), and its handler schedules appCtx.restart() 3 s later while the worker is still active (RegexExtensions.kt:51-58). The product reports the rule, disables it for the caller and keeps the original text. Both sides are recorded verbatim; the row is not normalized into a pass. The single call cannot demonstrate the restart, which is why it carries no compared value.
